axes.position: Usually defines constructs narrowly and operationally (a tractable sub-component like out-of-context reasoning, one cue, imitative falsehoods), while using broad behavioural batteries when probing emergent phenomena; more explicit about narrowness than typical.
Strongly driven by understanding surprising phenomena and open questions, often explicitly without practical application, more than the typical decision-driven eval builder.
Prefers controlled synthetic setups with matched controls and clean provenance, openly accepting toy settings and flagging realism as future work.
Uses LLM-generated, bulk-filtered data for training sets and many paraphrases, but hand-writes adversarial benchmark items when the target failure mode is specific.
Tends to evaluate default model behaviour with untuned prompts (zero-shot, no tuning on the benchmark), though finetuning is used as an elicitation tool for capabilities.
Mainly uses LLM judges over many samples, validated against humans, with human grading for early benchmark work.
Infers awareness from CoT articulation and behaviour rather than asking directly, but evidence is thin.
Samples many completions per question at temperature 1 and reports rates, rather than one sample per item.
No direct evidence on re-testing versus dropping near-miss results.
Often leaves unexplained puzzles to future work and publishes the phenomenon, but digs in with ablations and extra interventions when a core effect fails or is ambiguous.
No direct evidence on transcript reading versus breakdowns.
Routinely runs artefact checks and controls (random-articulation baselines, distractors, contamination cues), blending artefact hunting with confirmatory follow-ups more thoroughly than typical.
States general claims about the phenomenon but hedges consistently ('suggest', 'preliminary evidence') and lists limitations.
Consistently releases code and datasets publicly for reproduction and follow-up.

induced.name: Phenomenon-first vs threat-model-first question selection
induced.pole_a: Start from a surprising phenomenon or basic model limitation and derive safety implications afterwards
induced.pole_b: Start from a concrete threat model or agenda and design tests for it
induced.position: Picks questions by following surprising generalization phenomena, then demonstrates them vividly and leaves explanation and defenses open.

induced.name: Behavioural vs mechanistic evidence
induced.pole_a: Establish the behavioural phenomenon with black-box experiments and leave mechanism speculative
induced.pole_b: Ground claims in white-box or mechanistic analysis before publishing
induced.position: Relies on black-box behaviour via finetuning and output analysis, with post hoc persona or Bayesian explanations rather than interpretability.

induced.name: Finetuning synthetic facts as experimental medium
induced.pole_a: Finetune models on synthetic or implanted data to create controlled knowledge or behaviours
induced.pole_b: Study naturally acquired capabilities or behaviours in off-the-shelf models
induced.position: Builds model organisms by finetuning on fictitious facts, backdoors or narrow data to get clean provenance.

induced.name: Model access and scale
induced.pole_a: Run primary experiments on closed frontier models via finetuning API, replicate on open models
induced.pole_b: Run primarily on open-weight small models for activation access and many runs
induced.position: Usually uses frontier API finetuning for main results and replicates selectively on open models, though some collaborations use small open models.

induced.name: Release speed and framing
induced.pole_a: Fast early notes and vivid promotion with acknowledged limitations
induced.pole_b: Polished, thoroughly validated papers after broad coverage
induced.position: Posts early, hedged results quickly on timely topics and promotes striking examples.
